draft.title: Distributions of sample means
card: Take many samples of the same size from one population. Find each sample's mean, then plot all the means on a dot plot or histogram. This shows the distribution of sample means.
The spread of this plot shows how much the sample means vary.
When the sample size is larger, the plot is narrower. The means bunch more tightly.
Example: means of samples of 4 might range from 10 to 30. Means of samples of 40 from the same population might range from 18 to 22.
draft.remember: Plot many sample means to see their spread: bigger samples give a narrower plot.

a.q: What does each dot represent in a dot plot of sample means?
opts: The mean of the whole population
a.why: Each dot is the mean of one sample. A single value from the population is not a sample mean. The sample size is the same for every dot.
a.clue: The plot is made after finding a mean for each sample.

b.q: Mia plots 100 means of samples of size 10. She repeats it with samples of size 100 from the same population. How will the second plot look?
opts: Narrower, because there are fewer samples
b.why: Larger samples give means that vary less, so the plot is narrower. The number of samples is 100 both times, so it is not the reason.
b.clue: Compare the sample size, not the number of samples.
